deed: הרמב״ם כתב את משנה תורה — קודקס מקיף של כל ההלכה היהודית, בעברית ברורה
year: לא ידוע; הושלם ב-1180 או בסביבות 1178
title: Maimonides set out Jewish law in a single book in Hebrew: the Mishneh Torah, 14 books arranged by subject

trailer.text: Maimonides, a native of Cordoba in Spain, is considered, according to the National Library of Israel, one of the greatest Jewish thinkers and leaders of all time.
According to Chabad.org, before him, anyone who wanted to know Jewish law had to learn the entire Talmud.
By his own account, as cited by My Jewish Learning, he invested ten years of incessant writing and editing in the Mishneh Torah.

According to My Jewish Learning, the work comprises 14 books arranged by subject, and according to Stanford it is written in a fairly simple Hebrew that could be mastered after some study. At least, that is what Maimonides himself wrote to one of his readers who asked for an Arabic translation.
According to My Jewish Learning, the book was disseminated throughout the Jewish world within years, and for more than 800 years it has had no rival in its lucidity.

glance.label: Author
glance.value: Maimonides, a native of Cordoba in Spain

paragraphs.text: According to Chabad.org, Maimonides was born in Cordoba, Spain, on the fourteenth of Nissan, the eve of Passover, in the year four thousand eight hundred and ninety-five (1135).
According to Stanford, his father Maimon was a prominent rabbi, judge and communal leader.
According to Chabad.org, Maimon was a judge in the city's rabbinical court.
According to Stanford, the Almohads conquered much of southern Spain, and initially they were not tolerant of Jews and Christians.
According to the National Library of Israel, in 1148, following the Almohad invasion, Maimonides fled with his family to Morocco.
According to the National Library of Israel, some claim that during this period Maimonides converted to Islam to save his life, but continued to observe the commandments in secret.
According to Stanford, Arab historians relate that the Maimon family was forcibly converted to Islam, and many historians today accept this claim.

stations.title: Fez, the Land of Israel, Fustat

paragraphs.text: According to Chabad.org, Maimonides did not find a suitable place in Spain, and moved with his father and his younger brother David to Fez, Morocco, for five years.
According to Chabad.org, in 1165 he visited the Land of Israel, and then moved to Alexandria, Egypt.
According to Chabad.org, he settled in Fustat, which is Old Cairo, and lived there until his death.
According to Chabad.org, in Egypt he was supported by his brother David, a merchant who imported diamonds from India.
According to Chabad.org, his father, his wife and two of his sons died within two years, starting in 1166.
According to Chabad.org, in 1171 David drowned when his ship sank en route to India.
According to Stanford, Maimonides refused on principle to receive a salary from the community as its rabbi, for he believed that Jewish law forbade rabbis from accepting money.
According to Chabad.org, without his brother's support he began practicing medicine and struggled to support himself.
According to Chabad.org, in his fifties he was appointed personal physician by one of the courtiers, and later physician to Saladin, the sultan of Egypt and Syria.

stations.title: The first step: the Commentary on the Mishnah

paragraphs.text: According to Chabad.org, Maimonides began writing the Commentary on the Mishnah at the age of 23.
According to Chabad.org, the commentary was written in Arabic in Hebrew letters.
According to Chabad.org, it was the first commentary on all six orders of the Mishnah, and it can be described as a synopsis of the Babylonian Talmud.
According to Chabad.org, the Commentary on the Mishnah served as a springboard for his magnum opus, the Mishneh Torah.

stations.title: The problem: law scattered across dozens of tractates

paragraphs.text: According to Chabad.org, before Maimonides, anyone who wanted to know Jewish law had to learn the entire Talmud.
According to Chabad.org, to study the laws of Shabbat through the Talmud, one had to search through dozens of tractates.
According to Chabad.org, the rulings and commentaries were not organized in an encyclopedic, logical fashion, and so researching them was extremely difficult.
According to My Jewish Learning, Maimonides wrote that the upheavals of life in the Diaspora had prevented scholars and laymen alike from understanding the vast talmudic literature.
According to Chabad.org, he felt that the key tenets of the Oral Law were fading from memory, and therefore the time had come to write an authoritative work.
According to Stanford, after completing the Commentary on the Mishnah, Maimonides worked night and day for ten years on a comprehensive law code.
According to Chabad.org, at the age of 42, while working on the Mishneh Torah, he was appointed Nagid of the Egyptian Jewish community.
According to My Jewish Learning, he purposefully omitted source citations and removed all traces of talmudic debate.
According to Wikiyeshiva, he also wanted to write a book of sources, but he did not succeed in doing so.

According to Stanford, Maimonides wrote in a fairly simple Hebrew that could be mastered after some study. At least, that is what Maimonides himself wrote to one of his readers who asked for an Arabic translation.
According to Chabad.org, the Mishneh Torah is the only work Maimonides composed in Hebrew.
According to Chabad.org, the Mishneh Torah is a fourteen-volume work that sets out Jewish law in a logical, systematic way.
According to Wikiyeshiva, it contains 14 books, 83 topics and 1,000 chapters.
According to My Jewish Learning, the books are arranged by subject and encompass all areas of Jewish law, from torts to ritual worship.
According to Chabad.org, Maimonides was the first to index the entire Oral Law.
According to Chabad.org, he explains the bottom line of halacha systematically, clearly and concisely, without the tangled back-and-forth of the Talmud.
According to My Jewish Learning, the book also includes laws that do not apply after the destruction of the Temple or outside the Land of Israel, such as the laws of sacrifices and agriculture.
According to Stanford, in his work he instructs which foods to eat and which not to eat, when to exercise, and how to live a healthy life.
According to My Jewish Learning, Maimonides envisioned his work as a library of Jewish scholarship, and suggested that one who studied it would have no need of other books.
According to My Jewish Learning, in Sefer Ha-Mitzvot he enumerated the 613 mitzvot of the Torah and divided them into positive and negative precepts.
According to Chabad.org, the Bodleian Library in Oxford holds a manuscript (Huntington 80) of the first two books, Madda and Ahava.
According to My Jewish Learning, the Mishneh Torah was disseminated throughout the Jewish world within years of its publication, and drew immediate praise from many quarters.
According to My Jewish Learning, more commentaries were written on it than on almost any other halakhic work.
According to Wikiyeshiva, the commentaries are so numerous that a two-volume book was published as an index to them.
According to My Jewish Learning, the book did not become a definitive code or displace the classics, but it changed the landscape of halakhic study and practice.
According to Wikiyeshiva, Maran the Beit Yosef wrote in the introduction to his book that he ruled mainly according to three pillars of instruction, and Maimonides is one of them.
According to the National Library of Israel, Maimonides' influence on Sephardi Halakha was immense, and he is revered among Ashkenazi Jews as well, even though some of them disagreed with him.

According to Chabad.org, in the spring of 1984 the Lubavitcher Rebbe, Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, called for adding daily study of the works of Maimonides, and tens of thousands enthusiastically accepted the suggestion.
According to Chabad.org, many hospitals and schools across the globe are named after him.
According to the National Library of Israel, he died in 1204 at the age of 69 and was buried in Tiberias at his request.
According to Chabad.org, his grave in Tiberias is to this day a place of prayer and supplication.
According to My Jewish Learning, Maimonides encountered fierce opposition to the publication of the Mishneh Torah, mainly because of his new halakhic methodology.
According to My Jewish Learning, the RaBaD of Posquières was his most passionate opponent.
According to My Jewish Learning, others accused him of attempting to supplant the Talmud and of weakening the chain of tradition.

According to Chabad.org, his critics felt that he had gone too far in putting the Oral Law into writing, and that he had done a disservice to his audience by not supplying the sources for his rulings.

disagreements.question: How old was Maimonides when the Almohads arrived and the family fled?

versions.says: Chabad.org: the family was forced to flee Cordoba when he was thirteen
Stanford: the Almohads conquered much of southern Spain when he was around ten

disagreements.question: How long did the writing of the Commentary on the Mishnah take?

versions.says: Chabad.org ("20 Facts" article): seven years, and he completed it in Fustat
Chabad.org (biography article): around ten years

disagreements.question: When was the Mishneh Torah completed?

versions.says: My Jewish Learning: in 1180
Stanford: around 1178

disagreements.question: In what year did David, Maimonides' brother, drown?

versions.says: Chabad.org: In 1171
Stanford: In 1177
Chabad.org: Yes; after being appointed personal physician to one of the courtiers, he was appointed physician to Saladin
Stanford: No, he was not Saladin's personal physician, but one of the physicians who treated his family and his ministers

disagreements.question: In what year was Maimonides born?

versions.says: Chabad.org: on 14 Nissan 4895 (1135), following the traditionally accepted view
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: in 1138
Maimonides himself, in his colophon to the Commentary on the Mishnah as cited by Yeshivat Har Etzion: he was thirty in 1479 of the Seleucid era (1168), so born around 1138

disagreements.question: How old was Maimonides when he died in 1204?

versions.says: National Library of Israel: 69
Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: he was born in 1138, so he died at about 66

disagreements.question: In what year did David, Maimonides' brother, drown?

versions.says: Chabad.org: in 1171
Stanford: in 1177
Posen Library: around 1177
Chabad.org: yes, after serving as personal physician to a royal courtier he was appointed physician to Saladin
Stanford: no, he was not Saladin's personal physician, but one of the physicians who treated Saladin's family and ministers
Yeshivat Har Etzion: he was the personal physician of the vizier al-Fadil

unknowns.text: The sources do not state in exactly which year Maimonides began writing the Mishneh Torah, only the year of completion and the length of the writing
It is not clear whether Maimonides' family was in fact converted to Islam

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, בספר המצוות מנה הרמב״ם את 613 המצוות המסורתיות שבתורה וחילק אותן למצוות עשה ולא תעשה.
claims.quote: In Sefer Ha-Mitzvot, Maimonides enumerates the traditional 613 mitzvot of the Torah, dividing them into positive and negative precepts

claims.text: לפי Chabad.org, בספריית בודליאן באוקספורד שמור כתב יד (Huntington 80) של שני הספרים הראשונים של משנה תורה, מדע ואהבה.
claims.quote: Additionally, the Bodleian Library in Oxford contains a manuscript (known as Huntington 80) of the first two volumes of Mishneh Torah, Madda, and Ahava.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, משנה תורה עורר כתיבת פירושים רבים יותר מכמעט כל חיבור הלכתי אחר.
claims.quote: the Mishneh Torah inspired the composition of more commentaries than almost any other piece of halakhic literature.

claims.text: לפי ויקישיבה, נכתבו פירושים רבים כל כך על משנה תורה עד שהוצא ספר בשני כרכים שהוא מפתח לפירושים עליו.
claims.quote: פירושים רבים נכתבו על ספר זה עד כדי כך שמכון הלכה ברורה ובירור הלכה הוציא ספר שלם בעל שני כרכים

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, משנה תורה לא הפך לקודקס מכריע ולא דחק את הקלאסיקות, אך שינה ללא ספק את נוף לימוד ההלכה ויישומה.
claims.quote: Although the Mishneh Torah did not achieve the status of a definitive code or displace the classics of Jewish scholarship, it undeniably changed the landscape of halakhic study and practice.

claims.text: לפי ויקישיבה, מרן הבית יוסף כתב בהקדמת ספרו שפסק בעיקר על פי שלושת עמודי ההוראה, והרמב״ם הוא אחד מהם.
claims.quote: מרן הבית יוסף כותב בהקדמת ספרו שפסק בעיקר על פי שלושת עמודי ההוראה ואחד מהם הוא

claims.text: לפי הספרייה הלאומית, השפעת הרמב״ם על ההלכה הספרדית הייתה עצומה והוא מוערץ גם בקרב יהודי אשכנז, אף שחלקם חלקו עליו.
claims.quote: His influence on Sephardi Halakha was immense and he is revered among Ashkenazi Jews as well, even though some disagreed with him.

claims.text: לפי Chabad.org, הצעת הרבי ללימוד יומי ברמב״ם התקבלה בהתלהבות על ידי עשרות אלפים.
claims.quote: This suggestion was enthusiastically accepted by tens of thousands

claims.text: לפי Chabad.org, בתי חולים ובתי ספר רבים ברחבי העולם נקראים על שם הרמב״ם.
claims.quote: Today, many hospitals and schools across the globe are named after Maimonides

claims.text: לפי הספרייה הלאומית, הרמב״ם נפטר ב-1204 בגיל 69 ונקבר בטבריה לפי בקשתו.
claims.quote: He died in 1204 at the age of 69. At his request, he was buried in Tiberias.

claims.text: לפי Chabad.org, קברו של הרמב״ם בטבריה הוא עד היום יעד לתפילה ולתחנונים.
claims.quote: To this day, his resting place is a destination for prayer and supplication

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, הרמב״ם נתקל בהתנגדות עזה לפרסום משנה תורה, בעיקר בגלל שיטתו ההלכתית החדשנית.
claims.quote: Maimonides encountered fierce opposition to his publication of the Mishneh Torah, mainly in response to its innovative halakhic methodology.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, הראב״ד מפוסקייר היה המתנגד הנלהב ביותר של הרמב״ם.
claims.quote: Rabbi Abraham ben David (RaBaD) of Posquières was his most passionate opponent;

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, אחרים האשימו את הרמב״ם בניסיון להחליף את התלמוד ובהחלשת שרשרת המסורת.
claims.quote: Others accused Maimonides of attempting to supplant the Talmud and of weakening the chain of tradition.

claims.text: לפי Chabad.org, מבקריו סברו שהרחיק לכת בהעלאת התורה שבעל פה על הכתב ופגע בקהלו בכך שלא הביא את מקורות פסקיו.
claims.quote: His critics felt that he had gone too far in transcribing and elucidating the Oral Law, and had done a disservice to his audience by not supplying the sources for his rulings.

claims.text: לפי Chabad.org, כשהיה בן שלוש עשרה נאלצה משפחתו לברוח מקורדובה כשכת איסלאמית קנאית השתלטה על העיר.
claims.quote: At the age of thirteen, his family was forced to flee Cordoba when a fanatic Islamic sect took control of the city

claims.text: לפי Chabad.org (מאמר הביוגרפיה), בשנות העשרים לחייו החל הרמב״ם לכתוב את פירושיו למשנה, ואותם סיים כעשר שנים אחר כך.
claims.quote: In his mid-20s, he began authoring numerous volumes on the Mishnah, which he completed around ten years later.
